Chapter 9: Fostering Positive Influence and Leading with Integrity
You know, every one of us has the power to influence people around us—whether we're parents, friends, coworkers, or just active in our communities.
Social psychology actually gives us a window into how influence really works, and more importantly, how we can use it in ways that lift others up and help them grow.
At the heart of positive influence is trust. When people look up to you—when they see you acting in line with your values, day in and day out—they’re much more likely to listen and be inspired.
Influence isn’t about pushing or manipulating. It’s about setting an example, encouraging others, and being that steady presence they can count on.
So, how do you actually foster positive influence? There are a few gentle but powerful ways:
First, model the behaviors and attitudes you want to see. If you’re consistently respectful, kind, and honest, others will notice—and often, they’ll follow your lead.
Second, lean into encouragement and positive reinforcement. When someone does something well, let them know. A kind word or a simple “thank you” can go a long way, a lot farther than criticism or pressure ever could.
And third, invite others to participate. Ask for their ideas. Make people feel like their voice matters. When you do that, you’re not just leading—you’re building a sense of belonging and shared purpose.
Now, leadership isn’t just for folks with fancy titles. Anyone can lead by creating an environment where respect, openness, and honesty are the norm.
The best leaders? They’re the ones who really listen, who learn and adapt, and who always act with integrity—even when it’s tough.
Here’s something worth remembering: with influence comes responsibility.
Even the smallest actions—like making sure everyone’s included in a conversation, or standing up when something’s not fair—can create ripples. Those little moments shape the culture of a group, or even an entire community.
So, when you think about influence, think about the kind of example you want to set. Lead with integrity, and you’ll make a difference that goes far beyond what you might expect.
